content.title: How to watch Guardians vs. Mariners for free on AppleTV Plus today
content.text: Updated: Mar. 27, 2026, 6:45 p.m.Published: Mar. 27, 2026, 6:45 p.m.Chase DeLauter looks to build off a storybook Opening Day as the Cleveland Guardians face the Seattle Mariners on "Friday Night Baseball" today. Find out how to watch for free. (AP Photo/Lindsey Wasson)APIf you purchase a product through a link on our site, we may receive compensation.By Robert Fenbers, cleveland.comSEATTLE – After a thrilling victory in the depths of the night, the Cleveland Guardians look to replicate their success against the Seattle Mariners today on “Friday Night Baseball”. The first pitch is set for 9:45 p.m. Eastern (6:45 p.m. Pacific). Apple TV Plus is the only place you can watch this MLB game, and you can tune in for free.“Friday Night Baseball” is a weekly doubleheader MLB showcase; in addition to the Guardians-Mariners game, fans can also choose to watch the matchup between the Houston Astros and Los Angeles Angels, which starts at 8:15 p.m. (7:15 p.m. Central).Apple TV Plus offers a 7-day free trial. After the seven-day free trial, you can cancel or stay subscribed to Apple TV+ for $12.99 per month.Cleveland Guardians The Guardians (1-0) outlasted the Mariners, 6-4, in the season opener on March 26. Rookie Chase DeLauter notched two home runs in his regular season debut, while franchise centerpiece Jose Ramirez tallied two RBI. After suffering a franchise-low .226 batting average last season, Cleveland amassed 12 hits in the new campaign. Starting pitcher Tanner Bibee exited in the bottom of the sixth with right shoulder inflammation. He allowed three runs and three home runs on four hits with seven strikeouts in five innings of work. Closer Cade Smith recorded his first save of the season. Guardians players to watchJose Ramirez Ramirez picked up right where he left off in 2025, tallying two RBI to help Cleveland outlast Seattle in the season opener. Chase DeLauter The rookie was as advertised, belting two home runs, including one in his first at-bat in the regular season. Steven KwanKwan was quiet for his standards on Opening Day, failing to record a hit while striking out twice in five at-bats. Seattle Mariners Looking to build off a deep playoff push that brought them within eight outs of their first-ever World Series berth, the Mariners (0-1) fell short in front of exuberant crowd on Opening Day. Dominic Canzone homered twice, helping Seattle keep pace with the Feisty Guardians despite mustering just six hits on the evening. Starting pitcher Logan Gilbert went five and one thirds, allowing three earned runs and five hits with seven strikeouts. Mariners players to watchCal RaleighRaleigh, the runner-up for AL MVP last year, was kept in check with three strikeouts and a walk in the season opener. He led the Majors with 60 home runs in 2025. Dominic CanzoneCanzone was the focal point of Seattle’s offense, notching a pair of home runs on Opening Day, including one in the bottom of the seventh to cut the lead to 5-4. Randy Arozarena Arozarena notched a double, his only hit in four at-bats on Opening Day. Probable startersCLE Gavin Williams (0-0) vs. SEA George Kirby (0-0)Williams surged up the rotation with a potent 2025. He went 12-5 with 173 strikeouts, which was 27th in baseball. Williams’ 3.06 ERA was 13th in the Majors.Kirby figures to be a crucial component of Seattle’s stud starting rotation. He went 10-8 with 137 strikeouts last year, settling for a 4.21 ERA and 1.19 WHIP.
